question.text: Do dsdk.logic's truth tables, model counts, entailment verdicts, strong-Kleene partial evaluation and proof checker give the right answers, as judged by an independently generated oracle and an independent JS reimplementation?

competing_explanations.name: correct
competing_explanations.description: dsdk.logic is correct on the exercised inputs.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: Compared against the brute-force fixtures and recomputed in the browser by viewer/parity/logic.mjs.

competing_explanations.name: shared_convention_bug
competing_explanations.description: Code and fixtures agree because both use the same wrong convention (e.g. enumeration order, implication).
competing_explanations.how_addressed: Fixtures were generated by an independent script; analytic counts (2^n rows, hand-derived model counts) need no reference code.

competing_explanations.name: weak_oracle
competing_explanations.description: The comparisons would pass even if the code were wrong.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: Mutation check (implication as iff) must fail against the oracle; capture.mjs also tampers one value and requires the viewer to flag a disagree mark.

competing_explanations.name: js_echoes_python
competing_explanations.description: The JS side agrees only because it copies Python's numbers.
competing_explanations.how_addressed: The viewer recomputes from formula structures alone and never reads Python's answers when computing the JS column.

claims: 25 fixture formulas: truth tables, model counts, satisfiable/valid flags agree across Python, fixtures and JS.
Wumpus 2x2-corner KB has exactly 3 models; P12 and P21 are entailed safe, P22 is undetermined.
Affirming the consequent is semantically invalid (countermodel) and rejected by the proof checker.
Strong-Kleene examples give the documented KNOWN/UNKNOWN verdicts in Python and JS.
does_not_claim: Correctness for all formulas (finite sample only; see induction disclaimer).
Any claim about performance or large formulas.
That the Wumpus KB models the real game; only that the stated KB has these models.
The induction claims for all n: executed checks do not prove them. tracks/A1/PROOFS.md does.

input_snapshot.source: Repository fixtures fixtures/logic/formulas.json (25 formulas) and fixtures/logic/wumpus_kb.json (Russell & Norvig pit/breeze corner KB); formulas, KB and proof/partial/induction cases are authored inputs, not observed data.
input_snapshot.schema: formulas.json: cases[{name,string,structure,variables,size,truth_table,model_count,satisfiable,valid}]. wumpus_kb.json: variables, premises[{name,string,structure}], models, queries[{name,string,structure,entails,first_countermodel}]. Structures use {op: const|var|not|and|or|implies|iff}.
input_snapshot.missingness_meaning: There is no missing data. 'Unassigned' variables in partial-evaluation examples are UNKNOWN (strong Kleene: evidence insufficient), which dsdk.core keeps distinct from NOT_OBSERVED, INVALID and NOT_APPLICABLE; a countermodel of None means entailment holds, not that data is missing.

config.enumeration_order: sorted variable names, false before true, first variable slowest
config.canonical_string_grammar: formula := atom | '(' '~' formula ')' | '(' formula ' & ' formula ')' | '(' formula ' | ' formula ')' | '(' formula ' -> ' formula ')' | '(' formula ' <-> ' formula ')' ; atom := 'true' | 'false' | NAME ; NAME := [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* except true/false

deliberate_failures.name: mutant_implies_as_iff
deliberate_failures.description: A mutant evaluator that computes (a -> b) as (a <-> b) is run against the independent fixture truth table for implies_ab.
deliberate_failures.detail: mutant disagrees with the oracle on 1 of 4 rows: [{'a': False, 'b': True}]

deliberate_failures.name: affirming_consequent
deliberate_failures.description: The invalid inference (p -> q), q |- p. Semantically it has a countermodel; syntactically the proof checker must reject the modus_ponens step.
deliberate_failures.detail: countermodel={'p': False, 'q': True}; checker: step 2 (modus_ponens): requires Implies(p, q) and p, concluding q

parameters.enumeration_order: variables sorted ascending, false before true, first variable slowest

run_record.random_draws: none: the build is deterministic (exhaustive enumeration, no sampling). pytest's hypothesis tests draw their own examples inside the pytest run.
run_record.uncertainty: No statistical uncertainty: every value is exact (finite enumeration). The residual uncertainty is correctness of the oracle and of the shared conventions, addressed by the mutation check, the independent JS recomputation in the viewer, and the tamper control in capture.mjs.

view switcher and formula selector operable by keyboard (Tab, Enter/Space, arrow keys in select)
every result also stated in text; agree/disagree is a word, not only a colour
download-values link (data: URL of the packet)

result.statement: Within the exercised inputs (25 formulas, the 7-variable Wumpus KB, 5 proof cases, 13 partial-evaluation cases) dsdk.logic agrees with the independent fixtures and the JS reimplementation; the Wumpus KB has 3 models, P12 and P21 are entailed safe, P22 is undetermined; the invalid inference is caught both semantically and by the proof checker. Universal claims rest on PROOFS.md, not on these checks.
result.next_bounded_experiment: Seeded differential fuzz: generate 1,000 random formulas (fixed seed, up to 5 variables) and compare Python and JS truth tables, model counts and partial evaluation; record the seed in the run record. After A2 lands, run the same fuzz through the parser's round trip.

wumpus.grid_note: Cell Pxy: x = column, y = row; (1,1) is the bottom-left start cell. P31 lies outside the 2x2 grid.

countermodels.name: affirming_consequent
countermodels.description: From (p -> q) and q, conclude p. Invalid: p=false, q=true is a countermodel.

countermodels.name: modus_ponens_valid
countermodels.description: From (p -> q) and p, conclude q. Valid: no countermodel.

countermodels.name: hypothetical_syllogism_valid
countermodels.description: From (p -> q) and (q -> r), conclude (p -> r). Valid.

proofs.name: valid_modus_ponens
proofs.description: p->q, p |- q by modus ponens.

proofs.name: invalid_affirming_consequent
proofs.description: p->q, q |- p claimed by modus ponens. The checker must reject it.

python.reason: step 2 (modus_ponens): requires Implies(p, q) and p, concluding q

proofs.name: invalid_denying_antecedent
proofs.description: p->q, ~p |- ~q claimed by modus tollens. Must be rejected.

python.reason: step 2 (modus_tollens): requires Implies(p, q) and Not(q), concluding Not(p)

proofs.name: invalid_forward_citation
proofs.description: A step may not cite itself or a later step.

python.reason: step 1 (and_elim_left): cites step 1, which is not an earlier step (must satisfy 0 <= c < 1)

partial_eval.name: false_and_unknown
partial_eval.description: False AND x is KNOWN false whatever x is.

partial_eval.name: true_or_unknown
partial_eval.description: True OR x is KNOWN true whatever x is.

partial_eval.name: excluded_middle_unknown
partial_eval.description: x OR ~x is UNKNOWN when x is unassigned (Kleene does not see the two x are the same).

partial_eval.name: implies_self_unknown
partial_eval.description: x -> x is UNKNOWN when x is unassigned.

partial_eval.name: iff_self_unknown
partial_eval.description: x <-> x is UNKNOWN when x is unassigned.

partial_eval.name: and_two_unknown
partial_eval.description: x AND y with both unassigned: reason lists both.

partial_eval.name: partial_and_decided
partial_eval.description: x AND y with x=false: KNOWN false although y is unassigned.

partial_eval.name: fully_assigned
partial_eval.description: A full assignment agrees with two-valued evaluate.

partial_eval.name: const_only
partial_eval.description: A constant-only compound is always KNOWN.

induction.disclaimer: These are EXECUTED CHECKS on finitely many inputs. They do not prove the claims for all n or all trees. The proofs are in tracks/A1/PROOFS.md (Proof 1 by induction on n; Proof 2 by structural induction).

mirror.claim: mirror(mirror(t)) = t for every binary tree t
mirror.checked_scope: every binary tree shape with 1 to 7 leaves (exhaustive: Catalan counts 1,1,2,5,14,42,132)
